## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2018-05-07: Form-of TRA filed as Exhibit 10.1 to S-1/A
- 2018-05-23: Executed TRA dated as of IPO close, 85% of cash tax savings to pre-IPO holders
- 2018-05-29: 8-K reports IPO close and attaches the executed TRA as Exhibit 10.1

#### Goldman Sachs merger and terminating TRA Amendment

- 2021-09-14: TRA Amendment executed concurrent with the Goldman Sachs merger agreement, providing that no payments will be made under the TRA following merger consummation (negotiated payment of zero)
- 2021-11-04: 10-Q discloses the TRA Amendment in the tax footnote; liability remains recognized at $332.3M pre-close
- 2022-03-11: Final pre-close 10-K carries the TRA liability at $403.1M with the Amendment described as effective at close
- 2022-03-29: Merger closes; the TRA Amendment's no-payment provision becomes operative and the liability is extinguished

## Explanation

GreenSky executed an Up-C Tax Receivable Agreement at its May 2018 IPO under which it owed pre-IPO holders 85% of the cash tax savings generated by Section 754 basis step-ups on LLC unit exchanges. The TRA accrued substantively, with the recognized liability growing from roughly $261M at YE2018 to $403M at YE2021. As a condition of Goldman Sachs entering into the September 14, 2021 merger agreement, GreenSky and the requisite TRA beneficiaries signed a TRA Amendment providing that no payments would be made under the TRA following or as a result of merger consummation, effectively a negotiated termination at zero. The merger closed on March 29, 2022, at which point the Amendment's no-payment provision became operative and the $403M liability was extinguished; GreenSky deregistered post-close. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record, including the fact that the executed Amendment text itself was never filed as an EDGAR exhibit.
